identity.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models

problem.claim: Discover and apply sparse, interpretable causal subnetworks to explain and edit language-model behaviors.

gap.claim: Prior circuits use polysemantic, difficult-to-interpret units such as attention heads and neurons, limiting their suitability for many downstream applications.

contributions.claim: Introduces sparse feature circuits: causally implicated subnetworks composed of human-interpretable features.
Introduces SHIFT, which ablates features judged by humans to be task-irrelevant to improve classifier generalization.
Demonstrates an unsupervised, scalable pipeline that discovers thousands of sparse feature circuits for automatically discovered model behaviors.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish sparse feature circuits from prior circuits by using fine-grained, interpretable features and present methods for discovering and applying them.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SHIFT improves classifier generalization after ablating features judged task-irrelevant by a human.
The authors report discovering thousands of sparse feature circuits through an entirely unsupervised and scalable pipeline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces methods for discovering and applying sparse feature circuits.
Defines the circuits as causal subnetworks of interpretable features and contrasts them with prior polysemantic circuits.
Claims detailed understanding of unanticipated mechanisms and presents SHIFT for classifier generalization.
Reports an unsupervised, scalable discovery pipeline yielding thousands of circuits for automatically discovered behaviors.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a causal, interpretable representation with a concrete editing operation based on human judgments of task relevance.

lessons.interpretation: Interpretability claims become more actionable when connected to a specific intervention and decision criterion.
lessons.application: Frame an interpretability method together with an explicit edit, the human or automated relevance test, and the target behavior it is intended to change.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work only characterizes representations and does not support interventions or relevance judgments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluation datasets, baselines, effect sizes, or statistical conditions for SHIFT's reported generalization improvement.
It does not detail how causal implication, feature interpretability, automatic behavior discovery, or scalability are operationalized.
